title: Disjointness event fibers of the model map are singletons
statement: Fix $n \ge 1$, and consider the finite sample space whose points $\omega$ each consist of a distinguished coordinate $T \in \{1,\dots,n\}$, a pair of bits $x_T, y_T$ at that coordinate, and a labelling of every coordinate by one of the three disjoint-coordinate types (neither, left-only, right-only). From such an $\omega$ one reads off the generated coordinate-pair vector together with the pair of input sets $X(\omega), Y(\omega)$, and one records the model data $\mathrm{model}(\omega) = (T,\ \text{coordinate-pair vector},\ \text{the ignored label at } T)$. Then for every triple $z$ in the target of the model map, there is exactly one sample $\omega$ whose generated inputs are disjoint, that is $X(\omega)$ and $Y(\omega)$ are disjoint, and for which $\mathrm{model}(\omega) = z$.
hypotheses_covered: n is a positive natural number (finite index set of coordinates)
z is an arbitrary triple in the codomain of the model map (special coordinate, coordinate-pair vector, ignored label)
the counted samples lie in the disjointness event (generated X and Y sets disjoint)
the counted samples lie in the model map's fiber over z
